title: National Athletic Trainers' Association Position Statement: Fluid Replacement for the Physically Active (2017 update)
content: National Athletic Trainers' Association (NATA) Position Statement — Fluid needs during exercise are highly individual, driven by sweat rate (which varies with body size, exercise intensity, clothing, heat, and humidity), not a single fixed daily water volume that applies to everyone. A practical, individualized method: track body-weight change before and after exercise (each ~1kg lost ≈ ~1L of sweat fluid to replace over subsequent hours) rather than prescribing a flat number of liters for every person.

title: National Athletic Trainers' Association Position Statement: Fluid Replacement for the Physically Active (2017 update)
content: NATA Fluid Replacement 2017 — Both under-hydration (impairs performance, increases heat-illness risk) and over-hydration (risk of exercise-associated hyponatremia — dangerously low blood sodium from drinking far more fluid than is lost) are real risks; 'drink as much as possible' is not safe general advice. Product implication: hydration guidance in this app must consider exercise duration/intensity and climate as rough signals, explicitly warn against both dehydration and overdrinking, and point users toward body-weight-change tracking for a more accurate personal number rather than asserting one fixed liters/day figure from bodyweight alone.
